title: Tasks & Environments

body.text: Work in Codex is called a
Task — each task runs in its own separate environment
that clones the repo with its dependencies, so the AI can experiment with edits and run tests without affecting your real code.

example: "Task: 'Add dark mode to the settings page' → Codex opens an environment, edits the code, runs tests, and hands it back to review"

title: Why separate environments

body.text: safe (your main code doesn't break) and parallel (many tasks at once)
— every change must pass your review before it enters the real code.

example: "Run 3 tasks at once: fix a bug, write tests, update docs — each in its own environment, no collisions"

question: Where does a Codex task run?

options.text: In a separate environment that clones the repo
The AI can experiment with edits without affecting the real code
Because nobody can see the code

question: When can a task's changes enter the real code?

options.text: As soon as the task finishes
After you review and approve it
To prevent collisions and test safely

question: What do Tasks and Environments help with?

options.text: Organizing work and isolating an experimentation space
